subject: Add a second legend for NA values in scale_colour_gradient() or scale_fill_brewer() etc?

messages.author: 58a86ec4ae6b61fc
messages.subject: Add a second legend for NA values in scale_colour_gradient() or scale_fill_brewer() etc?
parts:
For example,

miss <- sample(c(NA, 1:5), nrow(mtcars), rep = TRUE) qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars, colour = miss)

How would one get a second legend object showing the missing values are gray?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Add a second legend for NA values in scale_colour_gradient() or scale_fill_brewer() etc?
parts:
Hi:

If you want NA represented in the legend, you can finagle the NA in
miss to become an actual factor level and then set the desired color
for it. Here's the basic idea:

library(ggplot2)

miss1 <- miss # Copy original vector
# Coerce missing values to be character (=> miss1 is coerced to character)
miss1[is.na(miss1)] <- as.character("NA")
miss1 <- factor(miss1) # NA is now a factor level

qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars, colour = miss1) +
scale_colour_manual(values = c(rainbow(5), "grey40")) +
labs(colour = "Value")

The choice of rainbow(5) for the first five levels is not an inspired
choice, but it illustrates the idea. There are any number of color or
palette choices from which you can choose.

FYI, in ggplot2 there is exactly one mapping to any single aesthetic.
More specifically, you cannot generate two legends or colorbars for
the same aesthetic.

Dennis
